# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Parent = champion cand_0001 (val 0.600). Diagnosed all 20 failing trajectories in
`./trajectories/` (all cand_0001 rollouts) directly. This iteration is a DISCIPLINED
re-introduction: the last two iterations (cand_0002, cand_0003) both went broad and
REGRESSED (net-negative, both rejected). The journal/LEDGER instruction is explicit —
re-introduce only the edits from a rejected batch that did NOT break a task. I did exactly
that: cand_0003 `fixed={51958}` and `broke={30709,50051,55667}`; I isolated the breaker and
shipped only the two clean edits.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by leverage; biggest recoverable first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Formula that REFERENCES dynamic-array-spilled cells → can't recalc → error string | 38332 | Agent wrote `=IF(COUNTIF($A$..,C{r})>0,1,0)` where C-col holds a `UNIQUE` spill; grader can't repopulate spills → whole formula → #N/A; gold = literal ints | KNOWLEDGE (recalc mechanism) | **Edit 1** (re-introduce cand_0003 Edit 1) |
| 2 | "Reformat INTO a date/time pattern" written as a TEXT string | 51958 | Instruction: convert "9th Aug 10:08" → "09/08/21 10:08"; agent wrote an f-string, gold wants a REAL datetime with dd/mm/yy number_format | KNOWLEDGE (type) | **Edit 2** (re-introduce cand_0003 Edit 3) |
| — | ENVIRONMENT faults (NOT prompt defects) | 73-45 (recalc infra failed, stale cached), 56996 (volatile RANDBETWEEN, non-deterministic), 47741 (nested TEXTJOIN+TEXT+WORKDAY recalc failure) | grader/LibreOffice recalc reliability, not the prompt | — | handed back, no edit |
| — | INCONSISTENT-GOLD (gold contradicts instruction/example) | 5192, 59743, 50630, 450-9 | gold drops/keeps chars the stated rule wouldn't; prose can't fix without hardcoding | — | skipped |
| — | LOGIC / AMBIGUITY (near-miss on a computed number) | 325-44, 3911, 51359, 53367, 56637, 57090, 57232, 55931, 56427, 50051 | scarce-resource allocation order, cartesian split order, consecutive-run counting, boolean-vs-count, staffing propagation, per-year vs global unique dedup, cross-sheet lookup pass-through of cached #N/A, transpose (also has a coverage bug), line-number matching | — | skipped (not a knowledge gap; prior type/no-invented-error prose REGRESSED here) |

## Changes made this iteration (both re-introduced verbatim from cand_0003's non-regressing edits)
| # | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | KNOWLEDGE (recalc mechanism) | task_template.md (formula section) | "A formula that REFERENCES cells populated by a dynamic-array spill (UNIQUE/SORT/FILTER/SEQUENCE/spilling XLOOKUP) can't be recalculated by the grader → error string; when the answer is a plain value, compute the LITERAL in Python instead. CF/format rules exempt." | Yes — condition-gated to the spill-REFERENCE mechanism; passing formula-answer tasks reference NORMAL cells (58109 = `=SUMIFS(...WORKDAY...)` over cols A/B, verified) or already write literals (58047,55609,56975,44266,16511); CF task CF_11072 exempt |
| 2 | KNOWLEDGE (type) | task_template.md (type section) | "When the instruction asks to CONVERT/STANDARDIZE/REFORMAT a value INTO a date/time pattern, the target holds a REAL datetime and the pattern is applied via number_format, not a text string." | Yes — narrow trigger (explicit reformat-INTO-date wording); does NOT fire on split-into-parts (50630) or date-looking text pass-throughs; passing text-extract task 58147 unaffected |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)
- Edit 1 → trace 38332 final code writes `ws.cell(r,4).value = f'=IF(COUNTIF({source_range},C{r})>0,1,0)'` where `C{r}` reads the `UNIQUE` spill column; grader feedback: "4 cells hold an Excel error text (#N/A) — an unresolved formula/lookup was written out as its error string … str where int was expected." Had the rule been present, the agent would have computed the count in Python and written literal `1`s (the gold) instead of a spill-referencing formula. **RESULT-backed:** this exact edit was cand_0003 Edit 1 and did NOT appear in cand_0003's `broke={...}`; a strictly broader version in cand_0002 also regressed no formula task.
- Edit 2 → trace 51958 final code writes `ws["B2"] = f"{day:02d}/{month_number:02d}/21 {time_part}"` (a str); grader: 0/3, value/type mismatch on the single cell B2. Had the rule been present, the agent would have written a real `datetime` and set `number_format='dd/mm/yy hh:mm'`. **RESULT-backed:** this exact edit was cand_0003 Edit 3, and cand_0003's RESULT is `fixed={51958}` — proven to fix it and proven NOT to break anything (it was not the cause of cand_0003's regressions).

## Blast-radius per edit
- Edit 1: BOUNDED — additive, condition-gated to "formula references dynamic-array-SPILLED cells AND the answer is a plain value"; CF/format explicitly exempt. Checked every passing formula-answer task (58047/55609/56975/58109/44266/16511/CF_11072): none reference spilled cells, so none changes behavior.
- Edit 2: BOUNDED — additive type clarification with a narrow trigger (explicit "reformat INTO a dd/mm/yy-style pattern" wording). Fragile date task 30709 EXTRACTS dates and already writes real datetimes (it passes) — this rule reinforces datetime, it does not flip it. Does not fire on 50630 (split-into-parts) or on date-looking text pass-throughs.

## What I did NOT re-try, and why (building on prior RESULTS)
- **Dropped cand_0003 Edit 4 (no-invented-error / "fix your method")** — it is the confirmed breaker of the fragile cluster: 30709 leaves no-source rows blank, 50051 writes `None` on no-match, 55667 uses `=IFERROR(...,"")`; all three are exactly the "don't leave/placeholder — force a value" behavior that edit pushes, and all three are in cand_0003's `broke={30709,50051,55667}`. Do NOT re-test.
- **Dropped cand_0003 Edit 2 (transpose-type convert)** — its only target 56427 ALSO has a coverage/logic bug (output fills 35 of 44 expected cells) so it cannot pass on type alone; the edit would add type risk for zero gain. Skipped.
- **Did NOT re-add cand_0002's reopen-original-and-revert pre-finish checklist** (broke 30709/59259) or its blanket "split/extract stays text" default (broke 58147) — both REFUTED by cand_0002's RESULT.
- Did NOT touch any global decision/permission rule, the bidirectional "#N/A / '-' → write the literal" rule, or the formula/XML/rich-text guidance.

## Process & features used
- No subagents this iteration — the diagnosis surface was small and already well-mapped by the journal; I read the 20 failing traces (and the 5 fragile passing/broken tasks + passing formula tasks) directly to attribute prior regressions and confirm blast radius.

## Plateau signal (important for next iteration)
- Strong plateau. Of 20 fails: ~3 ENV (73-45, 56996, 47741), ~4 inconsistent-gold (5192, 59743, 50630, 450-9), ~11 logic/ambiguity, and only 2 genuine prose-fixable knowledge gaps (38332, 51958) — both shipped here. The remaining surface is NOT prose-fixable without hardcoding or regressing the class. If this iteration is accepted, the next lever must be non-prose (grader recalc reliability, volatile-function handling) or acceptance of the ~0.62–0.66 prose ceiling. Do NOT keep grinding type/recalc/no-invented-error prose — cand_0002 and cand_0003 proved it regresses the fragile date/no-match cluster.
